svg.title: TOPAK D2 — Policy composition: admit ⟺ floor_permit ∧ ¬bundle_deny
svg.desc: Two tiers decide every admit over one frozen input. The floor, a verified evaluator linked into the mechanism, is the only tier that can permit. The bundle, per-request and signed, is asked only whether to refuse, and only after the floor permits. Composition is a mechanism constant, so bundle ⊑ floor holds for every bundle at every age.

text.tspan: Floor tier · Cedar, linked · the only tier that can permit

svg.text: Obligation (§2): an evaluator with a mechanized semantics; an implementation checked against it; a decidable comparison of two policy sets over a declared
schema (implies, equivalent, always-allows, always-denies, never-errors); resident and linked; minimal. Cedar meets it; the reference links cedar-policy 4.13,
the Rust engine, the shorter chain to the Lean model (§3).
A library, not a service: no process, no socket, no fetch. Text, schema S and values file compiled in by path; the replica refuses to start unless their bytes
Schema S enforced on every request: a non-conforming input is a deny. S changes only with a mechanism release (§4).
Any evaluation error is a deny: Cedar skips a policy that errors, so a skipped forbid would let a permit through.
A deny names its reason: the forbids that fired, or FloorNoPermit when none did (finding 10).
Evaluation: any satisfied forbid denies; else any satisfied permit allows; else deny.

text.tspan: REFUSE · fail-closed on both sides · never ordered, always recorded (ADR-0020)

svg.text: From the floor, and the bundle is never consulted: Floor([forbids that fired]) · FloorNoPermit (outside every envelope) · FloorError (any evaluation error, or input outside schema S).
From the bundle: Bundle(reason) for a deny, an error, undefined, an absent bundle, an unreachable bundle, or a revision other than the lease's. A bundle is never asked whether to grant.

One engine and one language, where the
bundle ⊑ floor survives D-0030-1: composition is a mechanism constant and does not depend on the floor's language. The reference declares neither degeneracy since 2026.10.01 (ADR-0030 A1, Batch 24).

bundle ⊑ floor for every bundle, at every age, of the composed decision. It is no longer something a bundle can fail; a bundle whose text permits more than the floor is inert, not inadmissible. Refinement is still
discharged at promotion, now by construction.
Containment is checked against the floor, and no bundle can weaken it.
Stale bundles are monotone-safe, with no refinement premise: local enforcement under partition survives, sound by construction (the same shape as the lease argument).
No cross-language check. Deciding refinement with an SMT solver over Rego needed a mechanized Rego semantics that does not exist; composition removes the need.
Floor tightening never invalidates a promoted bundle.
A bundle cannot establish that something is allowed: always_allows over the composed decision is not provable.
Over-denial by a bundle is a modeled, attributed local event (deny=all is F2, ADR-0028).
A bundle can narrow a floor exception, including break-glass (§5): a bad bundle can disable break-glass, a liveness cost, never a widening.
Two languages and two engines; the floor must fit PARC: no aggregation, no regex, no computed data.

Neither Rego → Cedar nor Cedar → Rego is in the archetype. A transpiler is a Build artifact whose output becomes the enforced floor, and Build is where the Byzantine threat lives: a silent mistranslation means the
proven text is not the enforced text.
Cedar's analyses compare Cedar with Cedar. A deployment that keeps a Rego floor declares D-0030-1.
